identity.title: Dual proximity-activated immuno-LAMP-CRISPR for ultrasensitive protein detection on an integrated microfluidic chip.

content.abstract: Sensitive detection of proteins is critically important in biomedical research, food safety, and environmental monitoring. However, conventional protein detection methods are typically heterogeneous and exhibit lower sensitivity than nucleic acid-based assays, rendering them unsuitable for on-site analysis of low-abundance proteins. Herein, a dual proximity-activated immuno-LAMP-CRISPR (DPILC) technology was developed for ultrasensitive detection of Listeria monocytogenes p60 protein. To improve the detection sensitivity in DPILC, the nucleic acid amplification template could only be generated through two consecutive proximity-activated extension events, which substantially reduced background signals compared with the single-extension approach. Moreover, the two extension reactions produced a longer template than the single extension, enabling coupling with LAMP technology and thus simplifying the assay workflow. To further facilitate on-site application, the dual proximity-activated immuno-LAMP was integrated with CRISPR/Cas12a and a gravity-driven microfluidic chip for contamination-free visual detection. The DPILC assay achieved a detection limit of 1 x 10(3) CFU mL(-1) for Listeria monocytogenes in 10-muL samples, with no cross-reactivity against six non-target bacteria, demonstrating excellent sensitivity and specificity. Validation in spiked pork, lettuce, and skim milk samples showed detection performance comparable to that in pure culture. By combining the advantages of dual proximity-activated extension, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based signal transduction, and pump-free microfluidic operation, DPILC offers a promising platform for ultrasensitive protein detection in resource-limited field settings.
